body:
#337 ships `test_it_stays_off_by_default`, asserting every `--remote-control` occurrence in `pdca.toml` is commented. On the template that is right. But the suite renders into instances (it even branches on `RENDERED`), so an instance that **enables** the seam — the entire point of documenting it — inherits a permanently red test and carries a local test delta forever. This instance runs Remote Control on all four interactive leaves (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#176) and had to adapt the test during the v0.56.0 update (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#195).

Two ways out, either fine:

- scope the off-by-default assertion to the unrendered template (`skipIf(RENDERED, …)`), or
- assert the **protective half**, which holds in both postures: the flag may ride `interactive = true` leaves only, never a headless argv — a headless leaf carrying it starts an interactive session with no human to reach and hangs the flow. The instance's replacement does exactly this: split the `[leaves.*]` blocks, and for every non-interactive block assert no uncommented `--remote-control` line.

The doc-phrase pins are good as they are (`APPEND` / "do not add a second" / `CLAUDE-ONLY` / "headless builder/reviewer must NOT carry it") — the instance's enabled-posture comment was merged to keep satisfying them.
title: test_remote_control_docs: the off-by-default assertion fails on every instance that adopts the seam it documents
